items.title: 🚀🚀 README for Hacktoberfest Participants 🚀🚀

labels.name: Hacktoberfest
labels.description: Issues that are good first picks for Hacktoberfest participants

items.body:
Welcome to Hacktoberfest 2022! endoflife.date is a simple informational (open-source) website that details the support lifecycles of various products. If you are interesting in earning [some swag](https://hacktoberfest.digitalocean.com/resources/participation) and helping this project, read on. Please read this document completely before filing a Pull Request.

Before you get started, get to know the project a little bit. Open [endoflife.date](https://endoflife.date) and browse around a little bit. Take a look at some of these recently merged PRs to get a better idea: [#1598](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/pull/1598), [#1603](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/pull/1603), [#1552](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/pull/1552), [#1596](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/pull/1596).

## About the codebase

endoflife.date is built using [Jekyll](https://jekyllrb.com/) - the Ruby static site builder that powers GitHub Pages. The site is built and deployed to [Netlify](https://netlify.com). Since the site is mostly informational, you _don't need programming skills to contribute to the project_.

## 👾 Recommended PRs and Changes

Here's some recommendations for good first contributions to the codebase. We've also made sure that there are enough details on linked issues for beginners to start working on them.

### 🆕 Release Updates

The bulk majority of PRs to the project are trivial release update PRs. You can see previously merged PRs [using the `release-updates`](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/pulls?q=is%3Apr+sort%3Aupdated-desc+label%3Arelease-updates+is%3Aclosed) label as a guide. If a new release has been made for a project that is currently being tracked on the endoflife.date website, we welcome PRs for updating the data around for that new release. If you make such a PR, here's a short checklist to follow:

- Have you updated _all of the release cycles_ that might have got an update?
- Has any previous release reached end of life? Does that need updating?
- If it's a new major release (which needs a new release cycle to be added), do we have a corresponding EoL dates for it?
- Is the page automatically updated? If so, our automation bot might beat you to it.

### 💅 Design and Layout Changes

If you're comfortable with SASS, Jekyll, HTML, Javascript - we're looking for some help around easy to fix design issues on the website. Make sure you've read through the [HACKING.md](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/blob/master/HACKING.md) file and setup the project locally before you start working on these.

Note that we are looking for good clean code, and unmaintainable hacks might be rejected. Make sure your changes align with the Jekyll Philosophy (for eg using SCSS mixings and Jekyll best practices).

Click through the following issues to read more.

- [Autofocus to search input](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/issues/367)
- [Hide old releases by default](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/issues/50)
- [Add Product Logo in the sidebar](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/issues/283)

The following require a better understanding of Jekyll and Liquid templating. A simple easy-medium-hard rating is here to help you decide as well.:

- [Update API to use ChangeLog template](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/issues/394) (Medium)
- [Generate RSS Feed for every product](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/issues/48) (Hard)
- [Add a Last Modified Date](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/issues/70) (Easy)
- [Support LTS Dates](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/issues/156) (Medium)
- [Support Dark Mode](https://github.com/just-the-docs/just-the-docs/issues/234) (Medium)

### 🦄 Adding New Products

The [Guiding Principles](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/wiki/Guiding-Principles) of the project state that "it exists to be useful to the readers". The more products we track, the more helpful we become. We're currently tracking 66 products, and we'd like to track more. Here's a list of suggested products that we think are worth tracking. File a PR for any of these! A few have links to upstream project websites to help you find the actual dates for these projects.

- [Azure Kubernetes Service](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/issues/133)
- Internet Explorer
- ~~Apache Tomcat~~
- iPad
- ~~Samsung Galaxy Phones~~
- [Plesk](https://www.plesk.com/lifecycle-policy/)
- ~~Linux Mint~~
- [cPanel](https://docs.cpanel.net/knowledge-base/cpanel-product/product-versions-and-the-release-process/)
- ~~VMWare ESXi~~
- ~~VMWare Horizon (#540)~~
- ~~VMWare Citrix (#540)~~
- ~~[Microsoft Exchange](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/plan-and-deploy/supportability-matrix?view=exchserver-2019), [more](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/enterprise/exchange-2010-end-of-support?view=o365-worldwide)~~
- Quickbooks
- Various [Forza Games](https://culturedvultures.com/forza-end-of-life-process/)
- Movable Type
- Apache Cassandra
- Apache Mesos
- Rancher
- ~~Docker~~
- Ceph
- Postfix
- Envoy
- ~~HAProxy~~
- ~~Apache (the webserver)~~
- Many other Atlassian, Oracle, and IBM products.

> (This list is based on personal observations, requests from users, google keyword research, and [this list maintained by @witchcraze](https://qiita.com/witchcraze/items/af8ac5da5948ff6a609e).

If you'd like to create a new page for something that is not on the above list - that's okay as well. We haven't had to reject a product so far, and doubt we will reject what you propose. Just make sure it is a _well known product_. We are open to accepting devices, frameworks, languages, operating-systems, applications, and pretty much everything that has a support lifecycle of some sort. If in doubt, ask us.

In creating a new page, make sure you read through [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) to understand the file structure, and go through a few of previously merged PRs [with the label `new-product`](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/pulls?q=is%3Apr+sort%3Aupdated-desc+is%3Aclosed+label%3Anew-product). Also, please read through the [Guiding Principles](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/wiki/Guiding-Principles) to make sure your writing style and content is good enough and matches the rest of the site. Reading these will help you get onboarded faster and make sure that your PR sees a speedy merge.

### 📝 Changelog Links

Not all of the products on the website have their latest releases linked to a relevant page. Usually this is the changelog for that release or a blog post.

See this issue for all the details: https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/issues/39

### Miscellaneous Contributions

We have issues labelled as [good first issue](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+sort%3Aupdated-desc+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22) for easy to pick up contributions. All of these have a detailed comment at the bottom telling exactly what needs to be done, and what skills might be needed.

If you'd like to suggest a new product to track, please create a new issue. Issues are also welcome if you have any suggestions for the website in general - around design, visibility, accessibility, usability for eg.

## 👩‍🎓 How to file a Pull Request

For most trivial changes (mainly release update and small content fixes), you can make these using the GitHub UI itself - just to to the relevant file and click the Pencil icon:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/584253/134509844-197cb6fb-5d6d-4d8b-bf0b-84d6f0cf6989.png)

Edit the file accordingly, then type a good title and description for your changes:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/584253/134510105-1efacea4-8044-4b24-ae83-237539442fb6.png)

Click "Propose Changes" and then review the changes you've made before clicking "Create Pull Request". If you still need to make more changes, create a "Draft Pull Request" by clicking the dropdown on the "Create Pull Request" button:

![](https://docs.github.com/assets/images/help/pull_requests/pullrequest-send.png).

You can change the PR from a Draft PR to a ready PR afterwards.

## ✅ Validating your changes

Once you file your Pull Request, Netlify will provide a list of checks for your changes. If one of the checks is failed, you can click Details and see through the errors, or one of the Maintainers will be there to help you soon.

If all of the checks pass, you can click the "Details" link on the "Deploy Preview" Status Check to see a preview of the website _with your changes_.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/584253/134535142-7d1170b7-16f4-4cd3-987e-e890b76098d5.png)

Click through, and validate your changes. Click all the links in the page you've changed and make sure they're not broken.

## 📑 Suggested Reading

Please make sure that you've gone through the Hacktoberfest [Quality Standards](https://hacktoberfest.digitalocean.com/resources/qualitystandards) and the [Participation Guidelines](https://hacktoberfest.digitalocean.com/resources/participation).

Additionally, we have the following documents which should help you get familiar with the project and the codebase. You don't need to read all of these, and we've linked these docs above in cases where you must read any of them.

- [HACKING.md](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/blob/master/HACKING.md) contains instructions on setting up the codebase locally with Jekyll. Read this if you're planning to make complex changes or setting up the project locally.
- [Guiding Principles](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/wiki/Guiding-Principles) - These help us make decisions around the content we have. If you'd like to make sure your PR gets a speedy approval, please read these to ensure your changes are aligned with the rest of the content. This is _especially important if you are making non-trivial changes_ that deal with the content or add a new product.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) - This walks you through the structure each product page takes, in detailed comments. Do read this if you are _adding a new product page to the website_.
- [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/blob/master/CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md) - This project follows the Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct, which you can read at this link. You must read this and agree to abide by this at all times in your interactions with this project and its community.

# ❓ Questions?

If you have any questions, please [create a new Discussion under the Hacktoberfest category](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/discussions/new?category=hacktoberfest). If you are picking up a new task, first check if there is already a PR for the same, and if not - [create a Draft Pull Request](https://docs.github.com/en/github/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/creating-a-pull-request) as soon as you can so others do not pick up the same task.

This issue is pinned and locked permitted to keep this clean for Hacktoberfest related announcements. Please [create a new Discussions](https://github.com/endoflife-date/endoflife.date/discussions/new?category=hacktoberfest) in the Hacktoberfest category instead.

items.title: Enhancement Request: Add Dark Mode to HTML5RotatingSquares
items.body:
**Description:**  

To improve usability and aesthetic appeal, especially for users who prefer a darker interface, add a dark mode toggle to the **HTML5RotatingSquares** project. The feature should allow users to switch between light and dark themes seamlessly.

**Why This Enhancement?**  

- Enhances user experience by providing a visually comfortable option for low-light environments.  
- Aligns the project with modern UI/UX standards.  
- Attracts more users who prioritize customization in their applications.  

**Proposed Solution:**  

- Implement a dark mode toggle button in the header or settings area.  
- Use CSS variables for colors to simplify theme switching.  
- Store the user's theme preference in `localStorage` to persist the choice across sessions.  

**Acceptance Criteria:**  

- A visible toggle to switch between light and dark modes.  
- Dark mode uses darker background colors and lighter text while maintaining contrast and readability.  
- The theme preference is saved and restored when the user revisits the site.  

**Mockup/Design Idea:**  

| Light Mode              | Dark Mode              |  
|-------------------------|------------------------|  
| White background with black squares | Black background with light gray squares |  

**Additional Context:**  

This feature will cater to accessibility and usability standards. It can be further enhanced with animations to transition smoothly between themes.  

**Labels:**  
- `enhancement`  
- `frontend`  
- `good first issue`  

**Assignee:**  
[@RJPalmer](https://github.com/RJPalmer)  

**References:**  
- [CSS Tricks: Dark Mode Toggle](https://css-tricks.com/a-complete-guide-to-dark-mode-on-the-web/)  
- [MDN: CSS Variables](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Using_CSS_custom_properties)

items.title: Small Improvements for Docs Page
items.body: This would be a good first issue for anyone looking to get started improving and contributing to OCaml.org. ### IFrame Titles Using [`pa11y`](https://github.com/pa11y/pa11y) to perform an accessibility audit on the https://ocaml.org/docs page using the [WCAG2AA](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG21/) standard revealed a some small improvement that can be made: - The videos (which are `iframe` elements) should contain a descriptive `title` attribute -- you can read more about this [from Google's lighthouse automation tool](https://web.dev/frame-title/?utm_source=lighthouse&utm_medium=devtools). Note that titles will also need to be added to the `fr` page. ### Mobile Layout Whilst using the page on mobile I noticed the buttons linking to the OCaml manual appear a bit oddly. Currently they overlap with the title of the following section leading to a somewhat confusing layout. This image should convey this: It would be nice if this was cleaner and well-separated on mobile, but retained its layout for desktop which I think works nicely.

items.title: Unlabeled buttons in application's interface and player activity
items.body:
Hey there,
I have been testing this application in my android TV and I just can say this is absolutely amazing. previously I have tried to use the web player (context: I am a blind user and rely in accessibility services to navigate through the interface) and a native application works way better than the web interface. I already switched to Jellyfin from Plex and the Android TV app.

However I just would like to ask, if possible, could you add labels to buttons in the application interface? Basically when opening a TV show, where you see options for playing, shuffle, playing next and stuff, all of those buttons are unlabeled, which makes my accessibility service to report all of those as "image button". Also, in the player activity the situation is about the same, all of those buttons are reported as "unlabeled" and that's basically all.

If you need more info, [Here is an article about adding information for accessibility services in android.](https://support.google.com/accessibility/android/answer/7158690?hl=en)
If labeled correctly, that would be basically the best thing we could have as an accessible media center software, as basically all others have some parts incorrectly labeled or unlabeled at all.
Thank you very much for the great project.

items.body:
Related to #44 

I ran through all the app screens and elements currently in place and documented those all below.

A few areas to highlight:

1. FxA web content is a bit inconsistently read and keyboards appear vs not (may be web content related not app)

2. The search/filter experience on the list view is not quite polished and as what I see in Android’s own interfaces (Settings screen was a good compare/contrast)

3. The Settings screen elements seems a little disconnected from each other so not as clearly connected/usable as possible

And some findings from the other accessbility review for content labeling #200 show up clearly here (reuse of labels or missing labels).

I will file a follow-up PR to document the test plan (in addition to whats already in docs).

- - -

The reading of on-screen interface items and objects. Testing for:
- All on-screen navigation and button titles are read
- All on-screen alerts and popovers (interrupting the interface) are read
- All labels and text elements on screen are read
- Interaction elements like input boxes and filters have meaningful instructions
- Links to open websites are clearly indicated and read
- Swiping left/right to select next/previous elements works usefully
- Interface scrolling is available where needed


### Welcome Screen (first run)

- App Name: “Lockbox Firefox Lockbox” is read :warning: (repetitive but screen is still being worke on)
- Tagline: “Take your passwords everywhere” is read
- “Get Started button” is read — “double tap to activate”
- “To use Firefox Lockbox...” is read
- “Learn more button” is read — “double tap to activate”

### Sign in to Firefox Accounts (web view: email)

- When opened, no default interface item is selected/read :warning:
- Button “X” to close is “unlabeled button” :warning:
- “Enter your email to continue to Firefox Lockbox...” is read
- “Edit box - Email” is read
- Keyboard does not appear when input selected :warning: (had to hit “Continue” for it to appear, but works OK on “Password” input..)
- “Valid email required” error is read
- “Editing edit box: Email” is read
- “Continue” is read (:warning: not described as a button)

### Sign in to Firefox Accounts (web view: enter password)

- When loaded, interface is selected and read
- “Password edit box: Password” is read
- Double tap on “Password” does show keyboard (unlike email, note above)
- “Keyboard hidden” is read upon submit

### Sign in to Firefox Accounts (web view: enter password second run)

- When loaded interface is not selected and read
- Double tap on “Password” does not show keyboard (unlike above) :warning:

### Sign in to Firefox Accounts (web view: confirm this sign in)

- When loaded, interface is not selected nor read :warning:
- When confirmed, interface is not selected nor read, transition is not announced :warning:
- “Continue button” is read — “double tap to activate”

### List View

- When loaded, “List” is selected and read :warning: (first item could probably be the “Lockbox All Entries A to Z” filter instead)
- Drawer is “unlabeled button” :warning:
- “All Entries A to Z” is read :warning: (not announced its a filter)
- “Alphabetically” is read - “double tap to activate” :warning” (doesn’t match label of “All Entries A to Z”? not useful to explain it will filter?)
- Double tap “Alphabetically” and no transition or explanation its already selected/used :warning:
- Unclear if possible to tap or close the popup filter :warning:
- “All Entries Recent” is read :warning: (useful title for the filtered view?)
- Search field announced as “button” :warning: (not descriptive)
- “Search your entries edit box” is read and keyboard activated
- “Button search clear text button” :warning: (clear button description is complex)
- Each list item can be navigated using left/right swipes
- Each list item is read with website and username
- “Double tap to activate” is read on each item
- When returning from detail view, filtered text edit box is read but the context (like “accounts”) is not read :warning:

## Detail view

- When loaded the web address (https://) is selected and read first :warning: (could be the nav bar title instead)
- Back arrow is “unlabeled button” :warning:
- Web address is read: “https://accounts.firefox.com edit box web address”
- Username is read: “faketester3 edit box username”
- Double tap on field does not copy to clipboard :warning: (expected?)
- Double tap copy buttons are read
- “Username copied” and “Password copied” alerts are read
- Password is read: “password 21 characters edit box password”
